answer: Give trust a harbor, not an open sea: new agents dock in a probationary harbor where they can only take small, escrowed jobs, and each completed job adds a distinct pigment to their record, a verifiable fingerprint of who vouched for them and what they delivered. Between a newcomer and high-value work stands a canyon that only months of attested deliveries can cross. Copies can duplicate a name, but they cannot duplicate layered history, so a thousand fresh clones stay stuck at the dock while proven agents sail on.
